conviction_note: The AGM trading update will be the first statement under new CEO Dean Banks. It covers a 17-week period whose last month carried the Your First Home deferral that Bellway warned about, plus the weakest mortgage approvals since 2023, and FY27 completion guidance was already cut on 16 Sep. Those lean negative. Against them: a crowded and still-building 9.13% short, and the name closed up after each of its last four trading updates, including +11.7% on the September guidance cut. So the findings sum to -1.2 while p_up sits at 48, giving a scaled -0.22 on a 5.5% absolute move. The gap between the two is the reaction function, which I expect to blunt the fundamental read rather than reverse it.

findings.finding: Bellway, the last direct peer to report (13 Oct 2026), showed its private reservation rate ex-bulk falling to 0.45 from 0.48 over the 9 weeks from 1 Aug. It also said the period before Your First Home launches 'may influence the timing of purchasing decisions' among first-time buyers. Barratt's 17-week window runs to ~25 Oct, includes the four weeks after the 28 Sep scheme announcement, and the launch has since been dated to April 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reservation-rate lines have not driven sell-offs here: on 16 Sep 2026 an underlying rate of 0.53 vs 0.55 came with a guidance cut and the stock closed +11.7%. The 5 Nov 2025 AGM update (0.57 vs 0.59) moved +0.86%.
findings.original_quote: While the Government's proposed Your First Home scheme has the potential to provide meaningful support for first-time buyer demand, the period ahead of its launch may influence the timing of purchasing decisions among some prospective customers.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector has been trading the scheme's headline (up ~9% on announcement, -7% on Budget detail), not the deferral effect on the autumn reservation run-rate, which no company has yet quantified for the post-announcement weeks. If it were priced, BTRW would not have recovered from 315.7 to 334.6 in the three sessions after the Budget. This is partly priced: it is a counterparty statement rather than Barratt's own number.
findings.independence: CBRE and the Vince Cable housing committee warned of FTB deferral ahead of the April 2027 start (https://mortgagesoup.co.uk/your-first-home-delays-could-stall-first-time-buyer-market/); Reuters on the April 2027 first loans (https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/british-homebuilder-shares-slump-lack-152736000.html)

findings.finding: The broad housing series covering Barratt's period weakened. BoE house-purchase mortgage approvals fell to 53,400 in September 2026, the lowest since 2023 and below the 58,800 six-month average (released 29 Oct). Nationwide's October 2026 HPI was flat m/m and +0.5% y/y, the slowest since Jan 2024.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Macro backdrop has been widely flagged in every Barratt statement since March and the stock has still closed up on its last four trading updates.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these series are public and the short register is building. The unpriced part is how much of it shows up in Barratt's own 17-week rate, and macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the release. Sized small and agreeing with the shorts, so it carries little weight.

findings.finding: FY27 completion guidance (17,500-17,900, set 16 Sep on a 45% forward-sold book vs 48% a year earlier) is at risk of a second cut or lower-end language. This is the first trading update under CEO Dean Banks (in post since 21 Sep 2026), after a period in which Bellway already guided its own FY27 volumes lower.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 16 Sep 2026: completions guide cut from 17,700-18,200 to 17,500-17,900 and the stock closed +11.72%, after falling from 309 to 276 into the print. 5 Nov 2025: guide unchanged, +0.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: A new CEO rebasing guidance at the first opportunity is a common pattern, but nothing has been said. The stock trades at 327.8, near the post-scheme range, not at the 276-290 lows seen before the September cut. If a second cut were expected, the price would sit nearer those lows. The case is inference from a company-level guide plus peer data, and the September cut may already have rebased the guide, so it is sized well below a realised cut.
findings.independence: CEO start date RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/barratt-redrow--btrw/confirmation-of-chief-executive-officer-start-date/9638046); Bellway FY27 guide down to 9,000-9,400 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/bellway--bwy/full-year-results/9819158)

findings.finding: Positioning skews the reaction upward. Disclosed shorts total 9.13% and are building. The name closed up after each of its last four trading-update or results days (+3.48% 15 Apr, +4.28% 15 Jul, +11.72% 16 Sep on a guidance cut, +0.86% 5 Nov 2025). Phoenix Asset Management crossed 5% to 6.52% on 15 Oct 2026, and the c.£386m buyback (about 8% of market cap) is buying daily.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Four of four recent updates closed up despite weak operating lines, the largest on a guidance cut, which is consistent with short covering.
findings.why_not_priced: The short register is itself the market's bet. The point is that a 9%+ short into a 'less bad than feared' print has repeatedly squeezed on this name. A long holder crossing 5% three weeks before the update is not reflected in the baseline's lean.
findings.independence: FCA aggregated short register 9.13% (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv); reaction history from Investegate RNS dates (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/BTRW)

findings.finding: Under the Budget's Your First Home terms, Barratt, as the largest UK builder, will pay the top 4% developer fee on scheme sales above 250 homes, against the ~1% the market expected (Peel Hunt). First loans are not due until April 2027, so the update will likely carry management's first read on participation and the margin cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BTRW -6.6% on the Budget day (28 Oct, 337.9 -> 315.7), then recovered to 334.6 by 2 Nov.
findings.why_not_priced: The fee is priced: the stock fell 7% on it. Barratt's own quantification is not, but its sign is unknown (it may stress the FY28 volume benefit), so the finding is near zero.
